pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.t: casa
examples.r: KAH-sah
examples.en: house

examples.t: mesa
examples.r: MEH-sah
examples.en: table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.t: hola
examples.r: OH-lah
examples.en: hello

examples.t: jueves
examples.r: HWEH-vehs
examples.en: Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.t: niño
examples.r: NEEN-yoh
examples.en: boy

examples.t: calle
examples.r: KAH-yeh
examples.en: street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.t: pero
examples.r: PEH-roh
examples.en: but

examples.t: perro
examples.r: PEH-rroh
examples.en: dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.t: gracias
examples.r: GRAH-syahs
examples.en: thanks

examples.t: café
examples.r: kah-FEH
examples.en: coffee

alphabet.title: The Filipino alphabet: 26 letters plus the glottal stop
alphabet.explain: Filipino writes in the Latin alphabet, but the alphabet officially taught in schools runs a to z without j, v, w, x and y except in borrowed words — and it adds the glottal stop (written ʼ) as a real letter of the language.

letters.tip: silent; marks the glottal stop: taʼo

counting.title: Counting in Filipino: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Learn 0-10 by heart. Eleven and up is labing-/labin- + the number below ten.
rules: All five vowels are pure: a e i o u, never diphthongs.
Final consonants drop in casual speech: bata sounds like bah-tah.
The glottal stop is real: taʼo (to be) is not tao (person).
